fields.title: جبل القارہ
fields.summary: نخلستان کے قلب میں وقت کے تراشے ہوئے غار، جو گرمیوں میں ٹھنڈے رہتے ہیں اور سردیوں میں گرم۔
fields.body: جبل القارہ (القارہ پہاڑ) نخلستان کے بیچوں بیچ کسی قدیم نگہبان کی طرح سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے، مگر اس کا راز بلندی میں نہیں، اس کے اندر چھپا ہے۔ چٹانوں کے بیچ غار اور راستے بل کھاتے چلے گئے ہیں۔ ان میں گرمیوں کے عروج پر خوشگوار ٹھنڈک رہتی ہے اور سردیوں کے وسط میں دھیمی گرمائش۔ اسی قدرتی مظہر کے باعث الاحساء کے لوگ قدیم زمانے سے یہاں پناہ لیتے آئے ہیں۔ پہاڑ کی تنگ راہداریوں سے گزریں، جہاں چٹانیں کندھوں کو تقریباً چھو لیتی ہیں۔ پھر اچانک راستہ اونچی چھت والے ایوان میں کھل جاتا ہے، جہاں روشنی کی ایک باریک لکیر چھن کر آتی ہے۔ چوٹی سے نخلستان یوں پھیلا دکھائی دیتا ہے جیسے کھجور کے درختوں کا سمندر ہو۔ یہی ایک منظر بتا دیتا ہے کہ الاحساء دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان کیوں بنا۔

practical.label: اوقات
practical.value: روزانہ 8:00–22:00 (چھٹیوں میں زیادہ دیر کھلا رہ سکتا ہے)

practical.label: فیس
practical.value: بالغوں کے لیے 50 سعودی ریال (SAR)، ٹکٹ “ارض الحضارات” (تہذیبوں کی سرزمین) سے ملتے ہیں

faq.q: جبل القارہ کب سے کب تک کھلا رہتا ہے؟
faq.a: روزانہ 8:00 سے 22:00 تک۔ چھٹیوں میں زیادہ دیر کھلا رہ سکتا ہے۔

faq.q: جبل القارہ میں داخلے کی فیس کتنی ہے؟
faq.a: بالغوں کے لیے 50 سعودی ریال (SAR)۔ ٹکٹ “ارض الحضارات” سے ملتے ہیں۔

faq.q: جبل القارہ کے غار اپنے معتدل درجہ حرارت کے لیے کیوں مشہور ہیں؟
faq.a: ان غاروں کا درجہ حرارت سال بھر معتدل رہتا ہے: گرمیوں کے عروج پر خوشگوار ٹھنڈک اور سردیوں کے وسط میں دھیمی گرمائش۔

faq.q: جبل القارہ کی سیر کے لیے بہترین وقت کون سا ہے؟

frame.det.hoursNotice: اوقات اور فیس میں تبدیلی ہو سکتی ہے، اس لیے جانے سے پہلے {op} سے تصدیق کر لیں۔
frame.det.report: کوئی غلطی نظر آئی؟ ہمیں بتائیں

changes.after: “ارض الحضارات” (تہذیبوں کی سرزمین) سے ملتے ہیں
changes.why: The only edit of this pass. «ارض الحضارات» is the place the reader has to buy a ticket from, and as written it is opaque: «حضارات» is not an Urdu word (Urdu says «تہذیب»), there is no Urdu attestation of the name (evidence E4), and the role file tells me to assume no familiarity with Saudi heritage institutions. One gloss, at the name's first mention in render order (the fee card), in the same device as the page's other gloss - title form first, Urdu in parentheses. It is a translation of the name the English source already carries («Land of Civilisations»), not a statement about what the place is, so no fact enters. The approved zh and ru cards likewise carry their parenthetical at this spot and leave the FAQ answer plain. The gloss is not repeated in faq[1].a (once per term per page).

tempted_but_not_added.what: A generic for «ارض الحضارات»: «ورثہ گاؤں “ارض الحضارات”» (heritage village).
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: This is what the reader most needs to know (what kind of thing sells the ticket), and the English card says it, as do the approved zh and ru lines. But the Arabic field gives only the bare name and the Arabic body calls it a project; stage 1 raised the divergence and it is unresolved. Writing village would settle it silently, so I added only the name's meaning.

tempted_but_not_added.what: Anchoring the first «نخلستان» to the place: «الاحساء کے نخلستان کے بیچوں بیچ» in the first body sentence (or in the summary).
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: Not a new fact - the body's last sentence and answer_en identify the oasis as Al-Ahsa, and the approved zh line anchors it at first mention. For a reader who does not know Al-Ahsa it would help. Left out because the phrase is the very construction P8 is about («الاحساء کا نخلستان» vs an izafat form vs the apposition «الاحساء نخلستان» that Urdu News uses), and it would add a third «کے» to the opening sentence. Offered to the judge together with the P8 ruling.

tempted_but_not_added.what: The 12-hour clock with day parts: «صبح 8 بجے سے رات 10 بجے تک».
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: It is the form this reader meets every day, and stage 1 already raised it. Not a fact but a format, and the termbase style rule fixes the 24-hour range form; changing it here would pre-empt that ruling.

tempted_but_not_added.what: Telling the reader this is a place for a hot day in the summary or under best time (for example that the caves are a cool stop in summer).
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: Heat is what this audience plans around, and the approved zh summary does add such a line. The source carries hot days only as a Good-for value, where the Urdu already has it («گرم دن»); moving it into the summary or tying it to «دن کے وقت» would be a new claim about when to come.

tempted_but_not_added.what: The figure of about 20°C all year round in faq[2].a, and the twelve named caves.
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: Arabic-only content; the source rule says it is not imported. It would make the mild-temperature answer concrete, so it is worth adding to the English field first.

tempted_but_not_added.what: A word for families: whether the narrow corridors and the way up to the summit suit small children or older relatives, and whether there is shade, seating or water inside.
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: Exactly what this audience asks, and exactly what the fence forbids: the source says only that families are a good fit and that the corridors are narrow. Nothing on access, effort or facilities stands in it.

tempted_but_not_added.what: How long a visit takes, and whether it fits a half-day from Hofuf or a weekend from Dammam or Riyadh; distances and driving times.
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: No duration, distance or route stands in the source.

tempted_but_not_added.what: A ticket price for children, or a note that the 50 riyal price is per person.
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: The source gives the adult price only.

tempted_but_not_added.what: A gloss on «ہفوف» (the main city of Al-Ahsa) or a line placing Al-Ahsa in the Eastern Province.
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: The role file says to assume no knowledge of Eastern Province geography, but neither statement stands in this page's source, and the area line is a card value with no room for running text.

tempted_but_not_added.what: Sharpening best time beyond «دن کے وقت» (morning, late afternoon, avoiding midday).
tempted_but_not_added.why_not: The source says daytime and nothing more.

notes.text: What this pass checked and found already in place after pass A, so left alone. Heat and season: the cool-in-summer, warm-in-winter property is the closing focus of the summary, has its own sentence in the body and its own FAQ answer, and «گرم دن» stands in the Good-for row. Hours as a planning constraint: the card, the first FAQ pair and the one-line notice («... جانے سے پہلے {op} سے تصدیق کر لیں») all say it plainly. Families: named first in the Good-for row. Register: a sightseeing visit is «سیر» throughout, never «زیارت»; no devotional framing, no «ماشاءاللہ» / «ان شاء اللہ»; no comparison with any other place; nothing about dress or access, because the source states none. Units and figures: nothing converted, nothing reformatted. Result: one gloss added, no sentence reordered, no emphasis shifted.

«جبل القارہ»: the single gloss is kept, in the body at first mention, not in the title, in the form stage 1 chose and stage 2 left: «جبل القارہ (القارہ پہاڑ)». Localizer's reading for the ruling: this reader very likely knows «جبل» already («جبل نور», «جبل احد», «جبل رحمت»), so on this page the gloss confirms rather than explains; it earns its place mainly by fixing the pattern for «عین», «قصر» and «سوق», which this reader does not know. The compact parenthetical is the right weight for a known word; the sentence-style alternative stage 1 offered («عربی میں “جبل” پہاڑ کو کہتے ہیں») would over-explain here. Form not changed, not settled.

«ارض الحضارات»: this pass adds a gloss, so the page now shows TWO KINDS of gloss and the ruling should name both. (a) Generic inside a name, rendered as a second name form: «جبل القارہ (القارہ پہاڑ)». (b) A whole name translated for meaning: «“ارض الحضارات” (تہذیبوں کی سرزمین)». Both use the same device (title or source form first, Urdu in parentheses). The termbase entry has gloss null and says the form is to be ruled in calibration; «تہذیبوں کی سرزمین» is therefore a proposal for that field, not a ruling, and I have not touched termbase.json. Rivals: no gloss at all (stage 1 and 2), or the generic «ورثہ گاؤں» (see tempted_but_not_added). «ارض» itself is familiar to an Urdu reader («ارض پاک», «کرہ ارض»); it is «حضارات» that needs the help.

The name occurs twice, never in the body paragraph: fee card (first in render order) and faq[1].a. gloss_regel says once per term, at first mention in the running text, never in a heading. A card value is not a heading, and a reader going down the page meets the name there first, so the gloss sits in the card. Two costs the judge should see: (1) the fee value now carries two parentheticals («(SAR)» and the gloss) and is the longest value in the card; (2) faq[1].a stays bare, and an FAQ answer can be read or emitted on its own. If the ruling prefers prose over card cells, the same gloss moves to the answer unchanged: «ٹکٹ “ارض الحضارات” (تہذیبوں کی سرزمین) سے ملتے ہیں۔».

The new gloss is written with the Urdu possessive, like everything else on the page: «تہذیبوں کی سرزمین» (izafat rival: «سرزمینِ تہذیب»). No izafat sign anywhere after this pass. The item bites one phrase harder than after pass A; «درجہ حرارت» x2 is unchanged.
Unchanged by this pass. «جبل القارہ» x6, «الاحساء» x3, «ہفوف» x1, «ارض الحضارات» x2, all byte-identical to the termbase keys.
Unchanged: three «الاحساء» tokens (body x2, area x1). The anchoring I held back (tempted_but_not_added) would have added a fourth.
Unchanged: plain alef in «الاحساء» and «ارض الحضارات»; the gloss adds no hamza-seat question.

Unchanged by this pass; the state is the one recorded in the stage-2 notes. Strings that depend on the gender of «غار»: summary (three agreeing tokens), body «چٹانوں کے بیچ غار اور راستے بل کھاتے چلے گئے ہیں۔» (the bare plural that can be read as a singular), faq[2].q. Independent of it: the body's temperature sentence and faq[2].a («ان غاروں کا ...»). From the reader's side: the Urdu this audience reads daily (Urdu News) writes «غاریں», so the masculine plural in the summary may look like a slip to some readers even though it is the dictionary form - worth a question to the blind reader.

Times stay in the termbase form («8:00–22:00»; «8:00 سے 22:00 تک»), currency stays «50 سعودی ریال (SAR)» in both places. Readers resident in the Kingdom know the riyal and read 12-hour times; both points are for the P7 ruling and the time-format ruling stage 1 asked for, not for this pass.

Because of the gloss, the fee card and faq[1].a no longer share the segment «ٹکٹ “ارض الحضارات” سے ملتے ہیں»: the card has the glossed variant, the answer the plain one. All other repeated segments listed in the stage-2 notes are still identical.

Not settled here and carried as stage 1 and 2 left them: heritage village vs bare name vs project for «ارض الحضارات»; the wonder/phenomenon decision of stage 2 («قدرتی مظہر»); «اس کے اندر چھپا ہے» for in its hollows; the loanwords «فیس» and «ٹکٹ» awaiting a termbase decision; the frame-string choices («سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات», «عمومی سوالات», «انتظامیہ», «کس کے لیے موزوں»). The stage-1 termbase proposal for «گوگل میپس» is carried below unchanged, since the string «گوگل میپس میں کھولیں ↗» is kept. No new proper noun was introduced by stage 2 or 3.
